# Branches the stale-branch cleanup never archives, and never deletes once
# archived. Read by .github/scripts/archive_stale_branches.py.
#
# One entry per line. A line beginning with "re:" is a regular expression,
# searched anywhere in the branch name -- anchor it with ^ and $ to mean the
# whole name, as the entries below do. An unanchored pattern matches more
# branches than it looks like it does, which errs toward exempting too many
# rather than too few. Any other line is an exact name. Blank lines and lines
# beginning with "#" are ignored.
#
# An entry added here after a branch has already been archived still rescues
# it: the archive copy stops receiving notices and is never deleted, and
#     git push origin archive/<date>/<name>:<name>
# puts it back. Restoring it is not automatic, on purpose -- adding a line here
# should not resurrect refs on its own.
#
# Protected branches and the head or base branch of any open pull request are
# exempt without being listed, so this file is for the cases neither of those
# covers. These are not preferences: every line is something that breaks if the
# branch moves, and the note above it says what, so the next person can tell a
# stale entry from a live one.

# Default branch, and the name it goes by in older clones and forks.
main
master

# The published documentation site. Deleting it takes the docs offline.
gh-pages

# Long-lived integration branch; several teams cut from it.
stable

# Release branches. 16 of these were already past 30 days on 2026-09-15, and
# being untouched for a year is what a shipped release looks like.
re:^release/.*$
re:^v[0-9].*$
